P1.text: Ship first, as one PR: port the untracked-callback rule so components with statements inline inside <For>/<Show>/<Match> callbacks and the render callback. Sound in Solid 1: mapArray runs each item in createRoot (untracked), Show/Match untrack a callback with a parameter, render uses createRoot. Targets no-host 15 + copy-no-host 9 on solid-ui and 2 on hackernews (Comment recursion stays).

estimate.unit: hours, ~25 solid-ui calls, est. 0.2-0.5 kB min

evidence.source: commit 632fb35 on solid-2-compiler, 1 of 9 commits in a ~3 h window

P2.text: Ship second: measure copies with the module's top-level constant data (4424b21) and fold constants exported from JSX modules (e59c432). On Solid 2 the measurement alone inlined Table and Card and cut the demo by 762 B gzip. It targets copy-size 286 and copy-shape 63, the largest decided-by-size buckets on solid-ui, though solid-ui has only 7 top-level array constants, so gain there is probably small.

estimate.unit: hours; gain on solid-ui est. under 0.3 kB gzip

evidence.source: roadmap.md item 11 on solid-2-compiler: demo 762 B smaller from this change

P3.text: Ship with P1 as cheap rider: fold define and import.meta.env in every build (a00bfc8) and replace constant memos (ff1bf8a). Both are small and independent. Measured pattern count in the example apps: import.meta.env 0, createMemo 2 on solid-ui, 0 on hackernews, so gain on these apps is about zero; value is for user apps with env flags and DEV branches.

evidence.source: grep counts on main examples

P4.text: Do not port the Solid 2 <For> unroll, <Dynamic> fold, or JSX-arrow reduction as headline work: the example apps have 0 <Dynamic>, 0 literal <For each={[...]}>, and 1 <For> over a constant list. The Solid 2 demo gain (-28..-32%) came from the whole app turning static so className/classList/effect helpers vanish; solid-ui and hackernews stay dynamic so that does not transfer. Port only the <For> unroll if time is left (about 1 h), because Solid 1 For has the same shape, but expect gains only in static-content apps.

estimate.unit: kB gzip on solid-ui, est. from 1 constant For

evidence.source: grep counts, solid2-benchmarks.md

P5.text: Biggest untouched bucket is copy-package 211 (Kobalte, Polymorphic x35) plus imported 468 on solid-ui, but the optimizer removed only 61 of 916 createComponent calls (6.7%) and most remaining calls are in package code the plugin does not see. Expand with the opt-in optimizer.packages copy (roadmap item 9) gated by the size estimate, starting with Kobalte's Polymorphic and ButtonRoot. Largest possible gain, largest work and risk (solid export condition, package public exports, hydration keys); ship as 0.5.0 experimental or defer to 0.6.0.

estimate.unit: hours; gain unknown, est. 1-3% gzip on solid-ui

evidence.source: grep -c createComponent on dist/default plain vs optimized in main-wt solid-ui

P6.text: Add a Solid 1 only target: member-tag (20 on solid-ui, 3 on hackernews). Context.Provider in the app's own code (FormControlContext.Provider x5, hackernews Context.Provider x3) could go through the existing provider-removal pass once the context binding is recognized; namespace tags such as dialog_exports.Content are Kobalte and stay out. Needs a read of provider.ts to confirm Solid 1 Provider semantics match.

evidence.source: main-solid-ui-reasons.txt and main-hackernews-reasons.txt

A1.text: Cheapest path to the same goal: release 0.5.0 as P1+P2+P3 only (about 3.5 hours, one cheap PR each), put the saved time into build speed and report coverage, and say plainly in the changelog that the example apps move by at most a few hundred bytes. Solid 1 example gains are 0.2-1.3% gzip and the machine builds solid-ui at 3.9-4.6 s; the leverage is build time (3.5x plain) and not bytes.

evidence.source: main-benchmarks.md

A2.text: Different lever: a pure post-bundle size pass is not needed; instead grow the gate. Lower the cost of the 'imported' (468) and 'copy-size' (286) decisions by revisiting default chunking: single chunking gives -1.3% on solid-ui versus -0.3% default, so a docs/default recommendation (CHUNKS=single or vendor split) gets about 1.8 kB more at no code cost.

P9.text: Only new lever worth a time-boxed look: props-use (56 calls on solid-ui). Registry components already follow the splitProps(props, [..]) + spread pattern the optimizer handles (104 splitProps in 22 registry files), so the 56 refusals are a specific unhandled read of the props parameter (inline.ts:687 and :703). Step one is to print those 56 reads from the main worktree and group them; build only if one group covers 20 or more calls, and ship only with a measured byte delta from OPTIMIZE=1 vite build on solid-ui.

estimate.unit: hours to classify, build cost unknown until classified

A3.text: If P9 finds no group of 20 or more, spend the remaining 0.5.0 time on build time instead of bytes: the optimized solid-ui build takes 3.9-4.6 s against 1.05-1.41 s plain, and the chunk renderChunk step is 34-41% of it (1.1-1.3 s). That is a measured, user-visible gain Q1 does not exclude.
